title: Fix the icons (13 October 2026)

hard_rules: Work ONLY in /projects/sandbox/.scratch/icons-work. Six other jobs push to the same master tonight; one of them (the Home screen job) edits native/ios views, so keep each fix small, rebase often and keep both sides on a conflict.

Touch only: native/ios/Assets.xcassets/**, native/ios/AppIconPreviews/**, native/ios/AppIcons.swift, the icon lines of native/ios/project.yml, single SF Symbol names in native/ios/*.swift, and your report docs/reports/evening-2026-10-13-icons.md.

NEVER open or view an image whose bytes you have not checked: run `file` on it first. A JPEG named .png once killed a whole chat session. Prefer checking pictures with tools (file, a Python PNG header read) over looking at them.

There is no iOS SDK here: parse-check every changed Swift file with `swiftc -frontend -parse`, and be strict about iOS 16 availability.

Push straight to master. No branches, no pull requests. Every commit message is one short line a person would write and ends with [skip ci]. Stage files by name; `git pull --rebase origin master && git push origin master`; retry if rejected.

items.result: Ten of the twelve fixed and checked with iOS's rounded mask: Knockout, Clay, Glow, Badge, Cloud, Ivory, Mint, Graphite and Sand lose their inner tile, rim and shadow (495733a) and Spectrum's pixel ring gets room on its own black (d095912); Cyan and Violet are left as they are because their art runs past the picture's own edges, so fixing them would mean drawing in parts that were never there (details in docs/reports/evening-2026-10-13-icons.md).
items.title: The 12 icons the owner circled (do this first)
items.detail: At 6 PM on 13 October the owner sent two screenshots of Settings, App Icon, with these circled in red: Knockout, Clay, Glow, Badge, Cloud, Violet, Ivory, Mint, Graphite, Spectrum, Cyan and Sand. What the screenshots show (confirm each from its real files, after checking the bytes with `file`): most of them, Clay, Glow, Badge, Cloud, Ivory, Mint, Graphite and Sand, and Knockout with its white rim, have their own rounded-square tile drawn INSIDE the picture, with a margin, rim, bevel or drop shadow around it, so on the phone each looks like a small icon sitting inside a bigger one, with a visible border or dark corners. Cyan is the opposite: its big C runs into the edges and looks cut off. Spectrum and Violet look wrong at the edges too: check for a frame, dark corners or art that isn't centred. Fix each so it looks like the good ones beside it (Lens, Reactor, Terminal, Gem, Storm, Saturn): the artwork's own background or face fills the whole square edge to edge, with no inner tile, rim, margin, shadow or corner showing, and the C and controller sit centred at about the size they have on the good icons. For a framed icon, crop or zoom into the inner tile's face, staying inside its rounded corners, or extend the face colour out to the edges. For Cyan, shrink the art onto its own background colour so the C has the same room as the others. Never recolour or redraw anything. Then make every size from the fixed 1024 picture with scripts/make-app-icon.py, make the preview in AppIconPreviews from the same picture, and build a before-and-after contact sheet of all 12 with iOS's rounded mask applied (check its bytes with `file` before viewing it) to confirm each one. If an icon cannot be fixed without redrawing it, leave it as it is and say exactly why in the report.

items.result: Every icon set, picture, preview and name checked out except one: the Default tile in Settings, App Icon showed a grey square with a letter D instead of the main icon, fixed in 47063ae by giving it its own 180px picture (AppIconPreviews/AppIcon.png, a byte copy of AppIcon.appiconset/icon-180.png) and drawing every tile from AppIconChoice.previewName.
notes_for_IC0_and_IC3: What was checked and found fine (no change needed): all 56 sets name 18 slots each, every named file exists and nothing extra sits in a folder; all 783 pictures are real 8-bit RGB PNGs per `file` (no alpha, no tRNS, CRCs good, nothing after IEND) at exactly their slot's size; every size in a set is the same picture as its 1024 (worst mean difference 0.23 of 255); no two sets are the same artwork; all 55 alternate previews are byte-identical to their own icon-180.png and to what build 184 shipped; the 55 names are identical and in the same order in the iPhone and iPad CFBundleAlternateIcons, ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_ALTERNATE_APPICON_NAMES and AppIcons.swift, and build 184's real Info.plist and Assets.car hold exactly those 55 plus AppIcon. Only nit: Line.appiconset/Contents.json lacks a final newline, harmless, left alone.

Tools outside the repo, in /projects/sandbox/.scratch/icons-tools (venv has Pillow, numpy, scipy): icon_audit.py re-runs every check above (`./venv/bin/python icon_audit.py`, expects 0 problems; it caught all 5 faults planted in a test copy). Re-run it after IC0 changes its 12 icons: it will flag any size or preview that no longer matches its 1024. car_facets.py lists the asset names in a built Assets.car. frame_check.py is an UNRUN draft for measuring inner tiles; check it before trusting it.
items.title: The home screen icon choices
items.detail: For the main icon and all 55 alternates: every file each Contents.json names exists; every file is a real PNG (check with `file`) at exactly the pixel size Contents.json says; every icon is opaque (iOS shows transparency as black); each preview in AppIconPreviews is the same artwork as its icon, at a sensible size; the names match exactly across Contents.json, project.yml (and the Info.plist it generates, CFBundleAlternateIcons) and AppIcons.swift; the picker lists every icon that can be set and nothing that can't, and the preview shown for each is the icon that really gets set. Fix every real problem without changing any artwork.

items.result: All 69 symbol names (106 uses, including ternaries, the PillButton and sessionButton/holdButton helpers) checked against Apple's availability list from SFSafeSymbols: only square.resize (Next resolution, in-game menu) needed iOS 17, swapped for arrow.up.left.and.arrow.down.right in 5b10c45; the app asks for no custom pictures by name, and every symbol is drawn at 9 to 17 points in sensible frames.
items.title: The icons drawn inside the app
items.detail: Every SF Symbol name used in native/ios/*.swift must exist on iOS 16, the app's minimum: a name that doesn't exist, or only exists on a newer iOS, draws nothing at all. Get an authoritative list of SF Symbol names with the iOS version each appeared in (for example the SFSafeSymbols project on GitHub, MIT licensed, which lists every symbol with its availability), fetched into scratch and never committed. For every name that doesn't exist or needs a newer iOS, use the closest symbol that exists on iOS 16, or wrap it in `if #available` with an iOS 16 fallback. Also check that every custom picture the code asks for by name (Image("..."), UIImage(named:)) exists in Assets.xcassets, and that icons sit at a sensible size where they are drawn. Parse-check every changed file.
